title: Sprint choreography and timebox alignment for regional runtime/console/api rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a region-aware, timeboxed launch choreography and calendar template that coordinates runtime, Console, and API surface rollouts. This ticket drives a prescriptive schedule (week-of cutover windows, freeze and blackout zones, and post-cutover stabilization) plus a lightweight orchestration checklist for cross-team execution. Goals: 1) minimize inter-region contention and capacity spikes during global launches; 2) provide a repeatable, low-friction calendar for product, engineering, SRE, and design to follow; 3) codify cutover decision criteria, canary ramp percentages, and rollback triggers; 4) produce a calendar-as-code template and a short-runbook for oncall and launch leads.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable calendar template (GMT-normalized) that defines staging, canary, regional ramp, and full-cutover windows across three regions (NA, EU, APAC).
Documented canary ramp table with timing, traffic % targets, key metrics to monitor, and abort thresholds agreed by SRE and runtime leads.
Runbook describing preflight checks, traffic-shadow plan, a post-cutover verification checklist, and communication protocol for rollback decisions.
Calendar-as-code artifact (YAML) that can be turned into intra-team calendar invites and integrated into the release conductor workflow.
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime PM, Console PM, SRE lead, and a representative from Customer Success for high-risk customers.
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Initial scope framed after sync with runtime and console PMs. Decided to include API surface in the same choreography to reduce cross-surface conflicts.

2026-03-11: Drafted timebox template (Confluence draft). Trade-off discussion: longer canary windows reduce risk but increase customer exposure; proposal set to 90min canary per region with a staged ramp to 25% over 3 steps.

2026-03-12: Engineering review (ENG-4021) notes kernel scheduling and autoscaler drain behavior could cause transient errors during the 3rd ramp step. Action: add a 30-minute stabilization hold between ramp steps and a pre-ramp capacity hedge lane.
2026-03-13: SRE provided abort criteria: increase in p50 latency > 25% sustained for 10m OR error rate spike > 0.5% absolute sustained for 5m triggers immediate rollback. Added to runbook.

2026-03-14: Design reviewed communications templates; recommended concise toast notifications to Console users + pre-cutover email to high-volume customers. Created draft email templates in Google Drive.

2026-03-15: PM owners aligned on calendar-as-code format. Created GH repo stub for calendar templates and a PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-templates/pull/12) with initial YAML schema. Next: finalize SLA-related blackouts and obtain stakeholder sign-offs.
notes: Recommended canary ramp (per-region): step 1 = 3% traffic (30m), hold 30m; step 2 = 10% (60m), hold 30m; step 3 = 25% (90m) -> full cutover after 60m stable.
Blackout windows: no major releases on local Fri 16:00 -> Mon 10:00 in each region. Global blackout exists for last business day of the quarter.
Capacity hedge: pre-cutover reserved burst pool equivalent to 20% peak traffic in each region for 2 hours post-cutover to absorb onboarding and cache-warm spikes.
Comms plan: pre-cutover channel (Slack #launches), 15-minute status pings during canary, post-mortem template and 72-hour stabilization watch.
Runbook links included in GH PR for easier traceability. Follow-up tasks: automate calendar invitation generation and integrate timeboxes into the release conductor signals.
